steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add celery and onion; stir until tender, about 5 minutes.

Mix in bread crumbs and parsley; remove from the heat. Stir in oysters, eggs, salt, poultry seasoning, thyme, and pepper. Add enough reserved oyster liquid to moisten mixture, stirring until well combined.
Transfer to the prepared casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden, and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Oyster Dressing (Stuffing)
raw_recipe.description: This oyster dressing (stuffing) recipe, with celery, onion, breadcrumbs, and spices, is full-flavored and a welcome alternative to traditional stuffing.

review.reviewBody: This is really good as is, and very similar to what I grew up with in Indiana. The only change I make is adding some chopped giblets from the turkey, along with a little broth they were cooked in. I've always used white bread because it doesn't compete with the delicate flavor of the oysters. If you never tried oyster dressing, try this one!

I came across this recipe and thought, "well, I can just use my regular dressing recipe and add the oysters." With that said, as far as the bad reviews (which are quite old I know), I wanted to mention that you can use your regular recipe with the oysters maybe adding some Old Bay or the like to spruce up that fish house flavor. I use homemade cornbread (a four inch skillet - about 3 cups of crumbs) with 16 slices of lightly toasted white bread food processed together. With all that bread you will need about 4 cups of stock, or the 2 cans of oyster juice plus stock to equal 4 cups, so that it is nice and moist and doesn't dry out in the oven. As for the stock, the turkey neck and giblets, heart, etc, do not get wasted in this house. Simmer those things in a potful of water with some celery and a bouillon cube or 2 - voila - stock. Makes a great gravy as well!

I made this but added my own stuff to this. I use dry bread crumbs and added turkey stock to make it moist not runny. Add poultry seasoning and sage, celery, onions, oysters and the giblets from the turkey as well. never used the juice from the oysters because I feel the juice made it feel slimy. I also sautéed the onions and celery in butter not vegetable oil. It turned out better than the recipe.

I made this stuffing for Christmas dinner this past year and my family LOVED it. My uncle asked if he could take the left overs home and my aunt emailed me asking for the recipe. The only thing I changed was that I added a tube of sweet thyme sausage that I ground and browned first, then cooked the onions and celery in the sausage fat that I drained off of the meat. The sausage made it really robust - almost casserole-like. Warning: it will make your entire house smell like oysters when you make this, so be prepared with good ventilation and lots of candles!

I really enjoy this dish and recipe. There's a good comment from another user that recommends adding 2 cups turkey/chicken stock and letting mixture stand 15-20 mins. I found those tips to be useful and make this dish even better. I also typically add 25-50% more oyster than what recipe calls for--we really like oysters!

I adapted this recipe to fit my needs. I had made an oyster dressing years ago where breadcrumbs were not overwhelming. To make this recipe work for me, I added only 1 1/2 cups fresh breadcrumbs. I used a 16 oz container of oysters with all its liquid. Baked at 325 degrees for 45 minutes. Delicious. It was so good I ate the leftovers for breakfast the next day.

This recipe is the way to go if you prefer moist stuffing as I do. It's the perfect foundation. The breadcrumbs are key to creating the start of the moisture as opposed to using cubed bread. From there you can add as much or as little vegetable broth as needed to achieve the moisture content you desire. Finally, spray on or drizzle some rendered duck fat and enjoy your own customized dressing. Enjoy!
Add chopped fresh mushrooms sautéed (I use 2 cups because family loves them) and put 2 turkey thighs on top when baking.

This is a pretty good recipe, but for 8 cups of bread crumbs (I used herb flavored), I added about 2 cups of chicken broth besides the oyster juice from 3 - 8 oz cans of oysters. You'll want to add enough liquid so that the stuffing is very wet, and give it enough time to really soak into the bread - about 15 to 20 minutes. You could easily add chopped turkey giblets, garlic and about 1/2 cup bell peppers for a little extra flavor.

Good starter recipe. I’ve been making oyster dressing for years now. I don’t know why you need eggs? Lol! I guess I should have a submitted my own version instead of riding another recipes tail! I actually took a few short cuts to this recipe. I used 2 boxes of stuffing mix instead. Substituted the water with broth on the box instructions and added sautéed onions and celery and added the oysters with the liquid then mixed it all up. And then baked the dressing just like this recipe instructs. There’s usually lots of left overs so I cut them like cakes squares and freeze those for later. Sometimes I freeze them in separate sandwich bags others I just freeze in gallon bags but try to keep them from touching until they are froze. This makes it easy when you only want one or two servings. And I apologize to the recipe submitter for posting my changes to your recipe.
I add all the liquid from the oysters and enough chicken broth to hold it together.

We loved this...thank you so much! Had to use canned oysters due to lack of availability of fresh (used 4 of the 8 oz cans, including the liquid as you suggested). Also dried my own bread by tearing up a 50/50 mix of white/wheat bread and baking at 300° for 10 minutes, then tossing and another 5 minutes. And you had mentioned adding seafood stock if necessary but we had preserved some homemade lobster stock and used that...a pint size jar was just the perfect amount. It took a little longer than 45 minutes due to our moisture level. But it got done before the turkey which was done in record time in our electric roaster (btw highly recommend if you never have...17 lb turk done in 2 hours). I just turned the oven off and left the dressing in until the turkey was done. Added a few pats of butter across the top to keep it moist but crisp y on top. Probably ended up being a little over an hour. Had a side dish of parsley potatoes using fresh parsley from my raised bed. The whole dinner was just fabulous. 😋
Should include amount of oyster liquid or stock to put in. Very dry and 8 cups of breadcrumbs is way too much, I only used half of of that and it was dry as dirt
It called for too many oysters.

Exactly the same recipe that my 1880's German Grandmother always made us, then my mom and then me. That being said, I have no idea if it was a German thing to add the oysters or my Grandad's side who were English/Pennsylvania Dutch but it was ALWAYS a part of our Thanksgiving and usually Christmas meals as well...she also made a great creamed corn casserole that featured oysters...I need another can! We always used the cans of Chicken of the Sea whole oysters for both recipes - try it, it might become your new favorite holiday dish~!
Followed the recipe to the letter, Excellent and so simple, every one loved it.
This was the most moist (added extra chicken stock) and flavorful oyster stuffing recipe i have made. Recipe is easy and results are excellent.
I followed the recipe but I added chicken broth and rubbed sage. It turned out delicious
I substituted veg oil for olive oil, added a cup of water chestnuts and a ½ tsp of sage. Came out great!
